column3: Release-only macOS dotenv template: app id, auto-update env, test release id, mandatory-update origins/JSON, Apple signing identity/team, CSC_LINK p12 + password, exactly-one notarization strategy, optional COS upload keys.

Release-only Windows dotenv template: app id, update env, mandatory-update origins, EV cert/signtool/key-container/PIN, optional signature-cache dir and 1-8 restore-worker concurrency, optional COS upload keys.
POSIX launcher that resolves its own symlinks, then execs the packaged Electron binary in RunAsNode mode against app.asar's dsh-desktop-host CLI with --expose-internals.
Windows counterpart of cli/dsh: sets ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 and execs "DeepSeek Harness.exe --expose-internals app.asar\dsh\node_modules\@deepseek-ai\dsh-desktop-host\lib\cli.js".
11-line C helper that creates the macOS command symlink with linkat(2) so the source inode is preserved and an occupied destination is refused.
Template for the private macOS signing file: signing identity, team id, relative p12 path, p12 export password, and the App Store Connect API-key notarization trio.
Production machine preset template: fixed app id, auto-update env=production, mandatory-update prod origin, pack concurrency, download/notarization proxies, optional signature cache dir.
Test machine preset template: app id, env=test, mandatory-update test origin plus allowedAuthOrigins JSON, download origin, 32-hex release id, concurrency and proxies.
Production Windows preset template: app id, env=production, mandatory-update prod origin, empty policy JSON, optional cache dir and cache concurrency.
Public Windows test preset template; deliberately holds no PIN or upload credentials, only the download origin, release id and policy origin.
Private Windows signing template: public .cer path, SignTool path, SafeNet key container name and token PIN, with relative paths resolved beside the file.
Type-only declaration of the electron-builder config shape the Desktop release tests assert, including the protocol, artifactName, nsis, win.signtoolOptions and hook signatures.
Five-line ordinary-release entry that re-exports the environment-independent config factory; qualification imports the factory without evaluating an ordinary release config.
Binary 2x light-theme installer brand bitmap (PNG, 40 KB); opened its header bytes (89 50 4E 47) to confirm it is a PNG, and it is raster artwork not read line by line.
Binary 2x dark-theme installer brand bitmap (PNG, 39 KB); header bytes confirm PNG; raster artwork only, so not read line by line.
Binary 1x dark-theme installer brand bitmap (PNG, 16 KB); header bytes confirm PNG; raster artwork only, so not read line by line.
Binary 1x light-theme installer brand bitmap (PNG, 16 KB); header bytes confirm PNG; raster artwork only, so not read line by line.
Binary uninstaller sidebar artwork (PNG, 10 KB) converted to a 164x314 BMP during preparation; raster artwork only, so not read line by line.
Header-only helper that formats a directory-replacement failure report: original Windows error, the operation attempted, source/destination, restoration error and preserved backup path.
NSIS macros that paint the rounded edit frame and the custom-painted launch checkbox with GDI+ while keeping the native control's state, text, keyboard and accessibility role.
Header-only parser for 7-Zip's refreshed ASCII progress lines, extracting a monotonically increasing percentage from a stream that may split numbers across reads.

Full failure-report toolkit: 7-Zip exit-code meanings, Win32 message formatting, headline extraction, UTF-8 decode with partial-tail trimming, bounded excerpt, file+clipboard output and a TaskDialog/MessageBox fallback.

Header-only 7-Zip driver: job-object and attribute-list child launch, UTF-8 error log, progress published through a window property, and a distinct negative-error range so Win32 failures never collide with 7-Zip exit codes.
NSIS installer lifecycle: DPI-aware frame setup, welcome/before-install/progress/finish callbacks, the native progress overlay, and a hard failure path that sets exit code 2 and quits.

Native welcome and finish pages: 96-DPI logical layout, brand bitmap swap for dark theme, custom-drawn buttons and checkbox, editable path with a 450 ms validation timer, and launch-through-the-user-shell handling.

Path validation and preflight: rejects drive roots, special characters, reserved device names, reparse points, protected system folders, and requires an empty or registered destination plus a writability and free-space probe.
Header-only progress model: 7-Zip drives extraction while the other stages use bounded exponential estimates, and only the successful NSIS finish callback may reach 100 percent.
Bilingual (en_US / zh_CN) installer strings for every native page and failure, including the disk-space, per-user, extraction-failure and copy-details copy.
Figma-derived light/dark installer palette in 96-DPI logical pixels plus the /THEME=auto resolution from the Windows AppsUseLightTheme registry value.

Windows data cleanup: normalizes and pins paths, refuses shell folders and the installation or protected Harness home, unlinks reparse points without following them, and keeps going past locked files.
Uninstaller data removal that targets the Electron user-data directory and the updater download cache, honours /KEEP_APP_DATA and ${isUpdated}, and never touches the Harness home.

Native x86 helper: DWM frame and shadow preservation, the GDI+ progress page with its own caption buttons, 7-Zip extraction, failure-report dialogs, process detection by full path, and directory-failure reporting.
Desktop manifest (0.2.1-rc.2, private, ESM): the ~35 packaging/upload script entry points, and the dependency split that forces the main bundle to inline workspace devDependencies.
Per-heading bilingual-pair hash record for the packaging README, pinning the English and Chinese blocks so the two must be updated together.

Build guide: release-version rules, machine presets, Windows/macOS Actions flows, the unsigned and local-macOS paths, macOS signing and cache policy, runtime file selection, and installation/release verification.
Chinese translation of the packaging guide; verified as a paired translation by its frontmatter and section structure, and it carries the same version table and command set.
Per-heading bilingual-pair hash record for the publication README.
Manual publication guide: deployment identity, the 32-hex test release id as a URL prefix, feed-before-YAML ordering, fixed latest downloads, DPAPI credentials, and the upload audit contract.
Chinese translation of the publication guide; verified as a paired translation of the English document.
Per-heading bilingual-pair hash record for the CI publication README.
CI publication guide: machine configuration layout, runner-label routing, GitHub Environment approval, the approval digest recheck, recovery from a pending tag, and channel restoration.
Chinese translation of the CI publication guide; verified as a paired translation of the English document.
Per-heading bilingual-pair hash record for the top-level Desktop README, covering all 26 documented sections.

Application reference: Electron-shell architecture, the bundled command runtime, installation ownership, the mandatory-update policy and its table of resolved fields, the update dialog and the local updater qualification.
Chinese translation of the application reference; verified as a paired translation of the English document.

Vector brand wordmark (15 KB SVG, 472x40 viewBox) whose glyphs are filled with CSS variables; read the header and first paths to confirm it is the light/dark aware brand mark, not logic to read line by line.
Shared foreground tint for full-window surfaces: 40 percent white in light mode, rgb(24 25 28) at 50 percent in dark mode, with the native macOS vibrancy owning the blur.
Embedded-shell frame bridge: a strict MessageChannel handshake (trusted event, parent source, dsh-app://app origin, exactly one port) that exposes status, subscribe and a request/response action API.
Styling for the mandatory-update dialog: muted status text, red error text, pill-shaped primary buttons, and a themed progress bar with its own webkit/moz pseudo-elements.
Alertdialog document with a strict CSP (script/style self only, no connect, no img) and a status region, an error region, a details disclosure and four action buttons.

Text-only renderer for the mandatory-update policy: derives title/detail/primary/status from the policy and update phase, maps a typed preparation failure to localized copy, and never lets the DOM authorize installation.
Login window placeholder that loads from disk before any network request, with a self-contained spinner and a CSP of default-src none; it declares no global of its own.
8-line static close-glyph SVG (two 14x14 paths); it is a fixed vector asset with no logic, so it was not read line by line beyond confirming its two-path structure.
Shared dialog styling: a 380px card, sticky action row, 44px touch targets, focus-visible outlines, a 150 ms fade with a @starting-style entry, and a reduced-motion override.
Dialog document with a strict CSP and a hidden focusable main element; the body carries the update-dialog class so the fade-in is driven by one visible class.
Ordinary update dialog: revision-guarded rendering, Escape maps to the cancel id and never to acceptance, a manual Tab trap over the real controls, and a single-flight responding flag.
Welcome-window design tokens and layout: Figma light/dark alias set, brand font, 600x700 grid, 240px action column, 440px key form, and per-platform hover and Reduce-Motion behaviour.
Welcome-window document with a default-src none CSP and a single #root, loading the shared brand font, welcome stylesheet and welcome script from ../lib/welcome.
Binary 1024x1024 macOS application icon (PNG, 279 KB); header bytes confirm PNG; raster artwork, so not read line by line.
Vector macOS icon source (7.3 KB SVG, 1024 viewBox, rx=230 rounded tile); read the header and first paths to confirm it is the inset macOS adaptation, not logic to read line by line.
Binary 1024x1024 Windows application icon (PNG, 128 KB); header bytes confirm PNG; raster artwork, so not read line by line.
Vector Windows icon source (7.3 KB SVG) whose whale group carries the id tray-glyph that render-tray-icon.ts scales; read the header and group structure, not every path.
Binary original 1104x1104 application icon (PNG, 369 KB); header bytes confirm PNG; raster artwork, so not read line by line.
Vector original icon source (7.3 KB SVG, 1104 viewBox); read the header and defs to confirm it is the unadapted whale artwork, not logic to read line by line.
Binary Windows tray icon (ICO, 15 KB, 7 PNG entries at 16-64 px); header bytes confirm an ICO directory with 7 entries; raster artwork, so not read line by line.
Builder child for qualification packaging: it verifies it is owned by its live parent via the version-scoped run.json pid, re-checks the signing interlock, and redacts credentials from any failure.

Per-user Windows PATH manager: a per-SID mutex, a JSON fingerprint of the PATH snapshot that must match before a write, ownership bookkeeping for the managed entry, and an environment-change broadcast.
Total deadline for one COS operation: wraps http/https so every SDK request inherits one AbortController, waits for request closure, and reports a TimeoutError.
Type-only declaration of the update deployment, channel, target and upload configuration plus the resolver signatures and their documented throws.

Resolves the deployment (test/production), the channel (nightly/latest), the target directory, the release-record and channel-metadata filenames, and the public URL and COS prefixes, validating every origin and release id.
Type-only declaration of the packaged commit, its dirty flag and the two environment variables that carry them.
Reads the checkout commit and dirty state once and passes them to every child process, because a build handed to a colleague is otherwise not traceable to its sources.
Type-only declaration of the per-target build directories, the target/platform resolution and the artifact output selection.
Resolves the fixed build target, gives each target its own mutable preparation and artifact directories, keeps the download cache shared, and selects the unsigned or unnotarized output directory.
Suggests the next build index by listing the published bucket (with an 8 s deadline and a complete-pages requirement) and falling back to local artifacts, so a published version is never reused.
Type-only declaration of the build-version resolver, its validator and the version-prefix helper.
Validates a build version against the product version, rejecting build metadata and requiring the test suffix shape, with a long comment on how electron-updater's semver comparison sees each form.
Type-only declaration of the bare-import policy, the bare-specifier test and the rolldown plugin that fails an unresolvable external import.
Rolldown plugin that fails the build when a Desktop bundle leaves a bare import the packaged application cannot resolve, reporting the importing module and every offending specifier.
Type-only declaration of the manual CI version resolver.
Resolves a manual CI build version from product/auto/manual mode, appending the UTC date, run number and attempt, and rejecting a prerelease on the latest channel.
Builds the COS client with retries, host switching, redirect following and clock correction all off, so an ambiguous write can never be sent to another endpoint.
Type-only declaration of the local macOS default environment, the machine-preset loader and the pre-flight validator.
Loads release settings from a file-owned dotenv or a machine preset, rejects unsupported keys and credential-bearing parse errors, and scrubs ambient release settings out of the parent environment.
Type-only declaration of the mandatory-update policy environment shape.
Resolves the deployment-selected policy origin, refuses origin or authentication inside the policy JSON, and requires nonempty allowedAuthOrigins only for the test deployment.
Classifies a publication failure into a safe code, message, HTTP status and request id, never recording the provider's raw response body or credentials.

Renders the Chinese pre-approval Markdown: environment, version, channel, platform, release id, installer and feed URLs, source commit, signature results, proposed tag, and the file list with SHA-256.
Zod-validated public publication config (bucket, origin, credential file path, optional macOS/Windows/GitHub-App blocks), with credentials read only after authorization.
COS transport restricted to the plan's exact keys, streaming reads and writes, forbid-overwrite on immutable binaries, and a re-read verification of every uploaded object.
Type-only declaration of the diagnostic that explains why a retained debugging package cannot be published.
Returns the Chinese rebuild instruction for an unsigned or unnotarized package, stating that the current artifact is internal-debug only and cannot publish or auto-update.
Channel lock (mkdir as a lock), durable publication journal, and a scan of retained journals that only counts newline-terminated entries when deciding a feed already completed.
Validates a publication request against GitHub run, job and manifest evidence, refuses a mismatched machine, and requires one unique runner label per configured machine.
Creates the desktop-v tag with the GitHub App installation token, refusing to move an existing tag and treating a 422 as a parallel create that must be re-read.
Reconciles remote bytes before changing a feed: supersede and conflict checks, put-intent/put-verified audit events, read-back verification, and a tag step that may leave the release tag pending.
Type-only declaration of the app id, npm registry, macOS signing identity and the three accepted notarization credential strategies.
Resolves and validates the public release identity: reverse-DNS app id, HTTPS npm registry origin, macOS signing identity without the Developer ID prefix, and one complete notary credential set.
Retains an immutable packaging attempt outside the checkout: a per-attempt lock, copy-then-rehash verification, a manifest, and an atomic rename that makes the attempt visible only when complete.
Tags the packaged commit after a production upload, never moving an existing tag, and reports the exact recovery commands when tagging fails rather than failing the upload.
Restores a historical feed under the caller's channel lock: verifies the historical binaries first, previews by default, and only writes the YAML, never a tag.

Probes the external tools a run will shell out to before it starts, exercising tar beside the archive and locating the Visual C++ build tools, so a missing tool is not discovered minutes into a build.
Builds the validated upload plan: reads back the packaging completion record, cross-checks the channel metadata, verifies each artifact size and SHA-512, and rewrites the feed URLs to absolute form.
Performs the upload with durable evidence: intent and confirmed events around every streamed single-attempt PUT, an input re-hash before each write, and a result.json recording the failing stage.
Development launcher: builds the workspace and shell, checks the built artifacts, prepares the disposable project and primary runtime, and launches Electron with the three inspector ports.
Prepares and registers a disposable Harness Dev.app for macOS, writing a launcher that exports the development home, the debug ports and the devtools flag.
Rebuilds the disposable npm project as links to the current workspace, mirroring pnpm's hoisted graph and the declared workspace closure so unhoisted plugins still resolve.
One-line re-export that imports the config factory without evaluating an ordinary release configuration.
The electron-builder factory: file lists, ASAR unpack rules, macOS entitlements and signing, Windows signer wiring, the four builder hooks, and the publish target.
Loads the POSIX flock native entry on first use, building native/system once when the addon or its JavaScript is missing, with a memoized loader that a failed load resets.
Builds the test-only signed builder configuration from the ordinary factory, overriding the app id, name, entry and feed so a qualification package cannot be mistaken for a release.
Fixed test-COS transport with a key allowlist restricted to the qualification namespace, a versioning check, streamed single-attempt writes, and a public readback path.
Checks the generated feed against the installer bytes and prepares a read-only binary and feed plan; it explicitly states that file integrity is not signature or authority to publish.
Type-only declaration of the qualification identity configuration.
Redirects the Electron user data, session data, Harness home and journal directory to a per-run location and refuses a package whose identity does not match the bootstrap.
Operator firewall fault for a test application: an owned-rule check, a typed confirmation, an executable-hash recheck, and a durable event record for each stage.
Verifies the extracted installer payload: ASAR identity, no links or unsafe paths, per-file hashes, updater dependency versions, the feed and publisher, and the runtime descriptor.
Supervises one operator-confirmed qualification build: refuses an existing signing interlock, hashes the tool inputs before and after, and keeps a fail-stop packaging record.

Separates immutable binary upload from fixed-feed publication: a revalidation against the verification receipt, a bucket-versioning check, a public readback, and a startup-evidence gate for the successor version.
Allocates a test run, validates its manifest identity on every read, parses the per-process journals strictly, and reconstructs the observed update flow without declaring it accepted.
Type-only declaration of the file hash and the two-source signature verification.
Verifies an executable with the real electron-updater verifier plus Authenticode, requires a timestamp, and re-hashes the file to prove it was not modified during verification.
Directory transaction: stage into .new-<guid>, back up to .old-<guid>, promote by same-volume rename, roll back on failure, and retry Windows errors 5/32/33 ten times with increasing delays.
Installer include: per-user enforcement, /THEME= parsing, brand and helper staging, the 7-Zip extraction callback, the running-application check, and the failure-report callbacks.
Single-key macOS entitlement plist granting com.apple.security.cs.allow-jit, used for ARM64 runtime binaries.
Type-only declaration of the notarytool adapter that splits submit and wait.
Splits electron-notarize's submit --wait into a timed upload and a timed wait, records the submission id and Apple status, and returns the rejected JSON so diagnostics survive.
Type-only declaration of the macOS updater feed and its write and verify operations.
Writes and re-verifies the macOS app-update.yml inside the assembled App, so a mismatched feed or cache directory prevents artifact promotion.
Binds a reusable thin Mach-O signature to the certificate, identifier, entitlements, tools and OS version, and refuses to reuse a signature for a universal binary.
Main and Helper macOS entitlement set: JIT, unsigned executable memory, disabled library validation and microphone input.

Temporarily routes Apple tools through the active macOS service under a per-user flock, saves the original settings, restores them after every lane settles, and leaves a recovery record on forced termination.
Type-only declaration of the macOS pack concurrency and the two stage-specific proxies.
Validates the pack concurrency and both proxy origins, and rewrites child proxy variables so an explicit download proxy bypasses only local hosts.
Signs and verifies every materialized Mach-O file with four workers, applying the JIT entitlement only to Node and the LibreOffice helper, and reporting cache hit and miss counts.
Installs and manages the runner LaunchAgent, generating the plist template in Node while rejecting newlines and template placeholders in every path.
Type-only declaration of the optional machine-owned macOS signature storage rules.
Validates the macOS cache directory as a real, unlinked, 0700, current-account directory, and never creates or repairs it during packaging.
Content-addressed macOS signature cache keyed by input bytes, mode and signing policy, with atomic publication, a one-GiB prune budget, and a fail-closed reader on eviction races.
Type-only declaration of the temporary macOS signing keychain wrapper.
Creates a temporary keychain, imports the p12, prepends it to the user search list, signs a probe to prove the identity works, and restores the previous list before deleting it.
CLI for cache migration, usage and explicit clearing, all under the account-wide signing-stage lock so no other writer can observe a half-migrated cache.
Four-line POSIX node shim that runs the packaged Electron binary in RunAsNode mode through DSH_DESKTOP_NODE_EXECUTABLE.
Windows counterpart of node-bin/node: sets ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 and execs the packaged Node with --expose-internals.
Two-key macOS entitlement plist for the x64 Node binary: JIT plus unsigned executable memory, which Rosetta execution requires.
Type-only declaration of the DMG notarization and verification entry.
Notarizes and staples a finished DMG, verifies it, and deletes the stale blockmap electron-builder wrote for the pre-notarized image.
Type-only declaration of the notarize-and-staple helper.
Wraps electron-notarize with the measured notarytool adapter inside a packaging journal phase, so acceptance and stapling checks stay with the library.
Operator entry for qualification packaging: a TTY-only typed confirmation naming the exact version and run id, and a refusal to proceed without it.
Runs the App and DMG notarization lanes concurrently on separate signed copies, verifies both before and after, and promotes the artifacts only when both lanes succeed.
The packaging orchestrator: target and host validation, mode flags, environment selection, the signed packaging stage with SIGINT handling, the ordered build sequence, and the release record.
Type-only declaration of the packaging run supervisor, its event recorder and the streaming redactor.

Supervised packaging run: credential-free event journal, a streaming redactor that hides secrets across chunk boundaries, process-tree termination on failure, and a timeout that fails the stage even on exit zero.
Type-only declaration of the in-process phase recorder and the redacted error formatter.
Records an in-process phase in the same journal as subprocess stages and formats nested errors with credential values removed, following the cause chain and aggregate errors.
Type-only declaration of the publication preflight.
Rejects a debugging artifact by name before any publication dependency is installed, pinning the exact packaging attempt.
Copies the platform launcher into the runtime cli/bin directory and makes the POSIX one executable.
Compiles the macOS command-link helper with clang for the target architecture and the Electron minimum macOS version, and refuses to run off macOS.
Materializes the production runtime: stage the package set, resolve the lockfile, install frozen, filter files, sign native code, write the descriptor, then smoke and re-verify.
Freezes the built shell files for a qualification version pair, hashing each input before and after the copy, and refusing links and special files.
Writes the per-run qualification entry point that configures the identity before the production main entry is imported.
Prepares one firewall fault plan bound to the verified version-1 executable hash, requiring a successful signature receipt and an in-run executable path.
Clones one verified runtime into two synthetic versions, rewriting the package versions and the runtime descriptor, and proving the source tree is unchanged afterwards.
Command dispatcher for the qualification tools: init, inspect, bootstrap, runtime, application, files and collect, each printing JSON and never performing a remote operation.
Validates the machine-owned macOS signing settings, emits the Actions log masks for every secret, and warns in the step summary when notarization is skipped.
Selects the local npm tarball closure rooted at dsh and the private Host, rejecting a workspace dependency that was not packed, and writes the package-set manifest.
Prepares the shared primary runtime for the selected target and runs its smoke checks, skipping them when signed Windows packaging defers execution.
Applies electron-builder's dependency-manifest cleanup before the runtime bytes are sealed, so the archived manifests match what the builder writes.
Stages explicitly classified Desktop patches into a disposable project, requires every workspace patch to be classified, and verifies the staged bytes against the lockfile.
Downloads and extracts the target Electron distribution, prepares the primary runtime, stages the CLI and command-link helper, and writes the runtime versions file.
Type-only declaration of the manual Windows CI version resolver.
Validates the Windows signing mode and machine preset, emits the Actions log masks, and records the version and step summary.
Compiles the x86 window-frame helper with the Visual C++ toolchain, optionally compiles the four native regression binaries, and converts the brand PNGs to 24bpp BMPs.
The CI publisher: verifies the retained package, destination and signatures, emits the approval digest, and then reconciles and uploads under the channel lock with a durable journal.
Operator entry for qualification publication: a TTY-only typed confirmation per action, with a local-only default that contacts no network.
Passes the GitHub App private key to the token action through GITHUB_OUTPUT with a random delimiter, after emitting the Actions log mask.
Renders the tray glyph at seven sizes from the vector source, scales it about the tile centre, and packs and unpacks a PNG-entry ICO with explicit dimension checks.
Selects one explicit successful packaging attempt from GitHub, requires exactly one successful package job, and maps the runner to a unique publishing label.
Verifies the retained package against GitHub evidence, checks the commit is still on the selected branch or tag, and requires configured environment reviewers.
Retains a completed CI package with its qualification, completion record and channel metadata, and writes the next-step instruction into the Actions summary.
Manual channel restoration: preview by default, execute only with an explicit flag, a reason, and a matching successful publication record.
Repeating Task Scheduler trigger that recovers an exited runner launcher, bounded by a restart budget that disables the task when exhausted.
Desktop-only omission rules for the immutable runtime tree: package-manager metadata, source maps, declarations, other-platform native binaries and test fixtures.
Explicit classification of every workspace patch as shared, workspace-only or runtime-only, with the reason for each, plus the reviewed dependency override.
Creates and validates the private macOS packaging directories, refusing linked ancestors and non-private ownership, and writes the preset templates.
Creates and validates the private Windows packaging directories on a fixed local drive with a private DACL, and copies the preset templates.
Signs the Windows runtime under the signing-stage lock with the content-addressed cache, then seals the runtime hashes and runs the smoke checks.
Drives the production NSIS directory transaction through nine failure modes, checking the exit code, the surviving version, the cleanup and the report contents.
Verifies the assembled application: the runtime descriptor, the Windows code signatures, and the packaged runtime smoke against the ASAR tree.
Runs the archive integrity check and the payload smoke under Electron RunAsNode, then the full Host smoke, with a private native cache.
Full Host smoke in a throwaway home: CLI plugin add and remove, the packaged frontend, a plugin route, a bundled-pnpm plugin install, and real DOCX/XLSX/PPTX to PDF conversion.
Runs the NSIS directory and replacement checks and then exercises both locked-file replacement modes against the compiled probe.
Checks the macOS toolchain and configuration, then runs the registered runner with a cleared environment, an explicit PATH and caffeinate.
Scrubs the environment to an allowlist, sets the machine configuration directory, probes every required tool, and starts the runner.
Runs the built Host update task protection in a private development profile with the model and telemetry plugins disabled and a 120 s deadline.
Drives the real Electron updater against a loopback server, checks the result and the screenshots, and retains the evidence directory.
Real signed and unsigned download qualification, with a bounded timeout that kills the whole process tree and records the outcome as JSON.
Builds an isolated payload through the production NSIS configuration and exercises the English and Chinese installer variants and the uninstaller.
Exercises the real NSIS publisher verification with four cases including a wrong-publisher negative control, and asserts the verifier was not skipped.
Runs the compiled Electron main entry against a private profile with the local update delivery and real Host IPC, with an optional interactive mode.
Uploads a validated target, optionally through the credential launcher, and records the production release tag only for a clean packaged commit.
DPAPI credential launcher: decrypts a CLIXML file, scrubs the child environment, redacts stdout, suppresses raw stderr, and clears the secure strings afterwards.
Verifies the installer bytes and its extracted payload, rejecting unsafe archive paths, links and duplicate Windows paths before any extraction.
Type-only declaration of the macOS signing and verification entry points, including the runtime and notarized-application checks.
Signs and verifies macOS artifacts, requiring the exact release authority, team id, secure timestamp and hardened runtime, and a stapled ticket with Gatekeeper acceptance.
Checks the installed Authenticode signature, the expected signer thumbprint and the presence of a signing timestamp.
Re-verifies the retained Windows or macOS artifacts at publication time: Authenticode with the configured thumbprint, or the DMG plus the app inside the ZIP.
Compares the complete archived dsh tree with the sealed inventory, including file membership, bytes and the executable flag of each entry.
Type-only declaration of the PE unpack preparation and verification.
Keeps prepared PE files outside ASAR without changing their bytes, and verifies the assembled archive holds identical unpacked copies.
Type-only declaration of the pinned NSIS directory installation adapter.
Patches the pinned electron-builder NSIS templates to stage and rename whole directories, preserving registration, uninstall UI and the signed bootstrap path.
Type-only declaration of the Windows signature-cache concurrency setting.
Validates the signature-cache worker count as an integer from 1 to 8, defaulting to four.
Installs and manages the Windows runner Scheduled Task, refusing to stop it while a worker runs and using a process-identity snapshot to kill only the owned tree.
Type-only declaration of the PE signature inspection, preservation, signing and verification surface.
Finds PE files by content without following links, preserves already-signed copies, restores from the cache in parallel, and signs the rest serially with verification.
CMD shim for SignTool that reads the signing inputs from the environment and clears them before invoking the tool, so the PIN never persists.
Type-only declaration of the Windows signing surface: environment builder, publisher resolution, token signer, scrubber, redacted error and the NSIS bootstrap hook.

The Windows signing gate: environment scrubbing, certificate and PIN validation, publisher DN extraction, the serial token signer, the dangling Authenticode directory repair, and the NSIS bootstrap signer.
Type-only declaration of the batched public-key verification.
Inspects up to 128 files per round in groups of 32 through at most four PowerShell processes, rejecting any missing, reordered or malformed result row.
Type-only declaration of the Windows signature-cache directory rules.
Resolves the account cache or a file-owned absolute local override, and validates drive type, ownership, links and destination permissions.
PowerShell half of the cache directory validation: fixed drive, no reparse point in the path, current-account ownership and a private DACL.
Type-only declaration of the content-addressed signature cache, its counters, the migration and the maintenance surface.
Content-addressed cache of complete signed files keyed by input bytes and signing policy, with a verified hardware-free restore path and explicit migration and clear operations.
Signs one newly compiled, never-executed probe before release preparation, verifying the timestamp and thumbprint, and refusing to run when an interlock exists.
Type-only declaration of the account-wide signing stage lock.
Serializes a complete signing stage under an account-wide exclusive Windows file handle, waiting on contention and recording the wait.
Type-only declaration of the hardware-signing interlock and its completion callbacks.
Acquires the one hardware-signing attempt slot before SignTool runs; only success releases it, and a failure keeps the interlock for administrator review.
Type-only declaration of the timestamp completion surface and its options.
Signs once, then timestamps fresh copies at most three times with bounded backoff, and publishes the result by atomic rename after byte verification, retaining evidence on failure.
